text: A friend's desktop is lifeless. She presses the button on the front and there is no reaction of any kind: nothing lights up, nothing spins, no sound.
expected: No power / PC will not turn on

text: There is a thin, high-pitched electrical buzz coming from the rear of the case. It gets worse when a game is running.
expected: Loud coil whine from PSU area

text: The metal box at the back where the power cable enters feels scorching hot, and you cannot see its fan moving.
expected: PSU overheating or fan not spinning

text: One of the memory sticks refuses to stay put in its slot: the little clips will not lock and it looks loose.
expected: RAM slot is damaged or does not hold the RAM

text: You fitted 16 GB of memory but Windows reports that only about half of it is available.
expected: RAM capacity showing less than installed

text: Several times a day Windows suddenly shows a blue screen with a sad face, and the error text is different each time.
expected: Random crashes or Blue Screen errors

text: You have just added extra memory. The machine powers up and the fans spin, but the monitor stays completely black.
expected: PC turns on but no display on monitor

text: Your computer begins to start, then reboots itself, again and again, and never reaches the desktop.
expected: PC keeps restarting in a continuous loop

text: When you switch the computer on it plays a pattern of short beeps and a small orange light stays lit on the board.
expected: Startup warning beeps or motherboard error light

text: After a few minutes of gaming the frame rate collapses. A monitoring tool shows the processor at an extremely high temperature and a lower clock speed.
expected: CPU thermal throttling under load

text: You have a sealed liquid cooler with a radiator. The pipes feel stone cold and silent while the processor temperature shoots up.
expected: AIO pump failure or no liquid cooling circulation

text: A scraping, clattering sound comes from the heatsink sitting on top of the processor.
expected: Unusual noise from cooler (rattling, grinding, or buzzing)

text: In the BIOS the cooler shows zero RPM, yet when you look inside you can see the fan turning.
expected: Cooler not detected or fan/pump headers not reading

text: Every fan in the machine roars at maximum all the time, even when you are only looking at the desktop.
expected: Loud or constantly high fan speeds

text: You swapped the old processor for a newer one and now the machine will not boot at all.
expected: PC won't start after installing a new processor

text: While fitting the chip you notice a few of the tiny gold-coloured pins in the socket have gone crooked.
expected: Bent pins or a damaged processor socket

text: Task Manager shows the processor maxed out all the time even though you have nothing open, and everything feels sluggish.
expected: CPU usage is always at 100 percent

text: The screen displays a floating message saying it cannot detect an input and then goes dark.
expected: Monitor says no signal

text: The picture keeps flashing and blinking on and off every few seconds.
expected: Screen flickering or blinking

text: Everything looks fuzzy and squashed, the icons are enormous and the picture does not fill the monitor.
expected: Blurry, stretched or wrong-sized display

text: You connected an extra screen next to the first one, but it stays black and Windows acts as if it does not exist.
expected: Second monitor not detected

text: Coloured vertical stripes run down the display and a small patch of pixels never lights up.
expected: Lines or dead spots on the screen

text: The charger is plugged into the laptop but the battery level will not rise and a note says it is plugged in.
expected: Laptop battery not charging

text: You press the power key on a notebook and it shows absolutely no sign of life.
expected: Laptop won't turn on

text: The underside of the notebook is burning and its fan sounds like a jet engine.
expected: Laptop overheating or fan too loud

text: You can hear a notebook running and its keyboard lights are on, but the display is dark.
expected: Laptop screen is black but the laptop is on

text: Several letters on a notebook's keyboard do nothing at all when pressed.
expected: Some laptop keyboard keys not working

text: Phones in the house browse the web happily, but your desktop says it has no connection.
expected: No internet on my PC

text: The wireless networks list has vanished from Windows and the option to join one is no longer there.
expected: WiFi option missing or WiFi adapter not detected

text: Other devices stream and download quickly, but this one crawls along on the same network.
expected: Internet is slow on my PC only

text: The wireless link keeps dropping out every few minutes and then reconnecting.
expected: WiFi keeps disconnecting

text: Typing and moving the pointer both do nothing; the machine seems to ignore you.
expected: Keyboard or mouse not responding

text: You insert a pen drive and Windows pops up saying it does not understand what was connected.
expected: USB device not recognised

text: A video plays on screen but you can hear nothing from the speakers or the earphones.
expected: No sound from speakers or headphones

text: Your printer is listed as unavailable and documents just pile up waiting.
expected: Printer is offline or not printing

text: During a video call the other people can neither see nor hear you.
expected: Webcam or microphone not working

text: You have about 60,000 rupees and want to assemble a machine mainly to play games.
expected: Build a gaming PC on a budget

text: A student wants a computer for programming and assignments and does not have much money.
expected: Build a PC for coding and college work

text: You want to cut videos and design posters. Where should the money go?
expected: Build a PC for video editing or design

text: Is it smarter to purchase a ready-made computer from a shop or put one together yourself?
expected: Should I buy a prebuilt PC or build my own?

text: You have never assembled a computer. Which component deserves the biggest slice of your budget?
expected: First-time PC builder: where should the money go?

text: You bought new memory sticks online and want to be sure they suit the board you already have.
expected: Will this RAM work with my motherboard?

text: Can the new chip you found fit and run on the board that is already in your case?
expected: Will this processor work with my motherboard?

text: You want a particular video card. Will it physically fit in your case and function with your machine?
expected: Will this graphics card fit and run in my PC?

text: You want to add a slim modern storage stick to an older computer. Will it be accepted?
expected: Will this SSD work in my PC?

text: You are eyeing a huge tower-shaped heatsink. Will it clear the side panel and suit your chip?
expected: Will this CPU cooler fit my PC and processor?

text: You own a 450 watt unit and plan to add hungrier components. Will it cope?
expected: Is my power supply strong enough for my parts?

text: Your six-year-old computer: is it able to run the newest version of Windows?
expected: Can my old PC run Windows 11?

text: Your computer has become sluggish. What is the single most worthwhile part to replace first?
expected: My PC feels slow — what should I upgrade first?

text: You only have money for one improvement for gaming: the processor or the video card?
expected: Should I upgrade my CPU or GPU first for gaming?

text: You have 8 GB of memory. Is that enough, or would extra help?
expected: Should I add more RAM?

text: Your computer still boots from an old spinning disk. Is replacing it with a flash drive worth the cost?
expected: Is switching from a hard drive to an SSD worth it?

text: Would a recent video card perform properly inside a ten-year-old machine?
expected: Will a new graphics card work well with my old PC?

text: Should you pour money into an ageing computer or just replace the whole thing?
expected: Is my old PC worth upgrading or should I buy a new one?

text: Can you improve a notebook by swapping some of its parts?
expected: Can I upgrade my laptop?

text: How frequently does the dust have to be removed from a computer?
expected: How often should I clean my PC?

text: You want to get the dirt out of the case without breaking anything.
expected: How do I safely clean the inside of my PC?

text: After how long does the grey compound between the chip and heatsink need renewing?
expected: When should I replace thermal paste?

text: How can you make sure your photos and documents survive if the drive dies?
expected: How do I keep my files safe and back up my data?

text: What is the careful way to keep the operating system and hardware software current?
expected: How do I keep drivers and Windows updated safely?

text: It is peak summer and the room is boiling. How do you stop the machine from suffering?
expected: How do I keep my PC cool in hot weather?

text: Where you live the electricity often cuts out or surges. How do you shield the computer?
expected: How do I protect my PC from power cuts and voltage fluctuations?

text: Ask the assistant something that has nothing to do with computers, such as today's weather or a recipe.
Ask the assistant for a joke or a bit of general trivia.
Ask about a problem with a mobile phone, for example a cracked screen.
Ask about a games console that will not start up.
Ask something about cooking or sport results.
Ask for advice on choosing a mobile phone plan.
